name: British Virgin Islands

registry.name: BVI Financial Services Commission (Registry of Corporate Affairs)

support.name: Department of Trade and Consumer Affairs

legalStatuses.label: Sole trader (registered business)
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.
legalStatuses.registeredAt: BVI Financial Services Commission (Registry of Corporate Affairs)
legalStatuses.feeNote: The Department of Trade and Consumer Affairs quotes the trade licence fee for your activity.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.registeredAt: BVI Financial Services Commission (Registry of Corporate Affairs)
legalStatuses.feeNote: A company costs more to set up than a sole trader business. The Registry of Corporate Affairs quotes the current fees.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
Incorporate the company with the Registry of Corporate Affairs
launchSteps.plain: Only needed for a limited company.

launchSteps.label: Get your trade licence
launchSteps.plain: Most businesses need a licence for their activity from the Department of Trade and Consumer Affairs.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Inland Revenue Department within 30 days
launchSteps.plain: This registers you for payroll tax. Self-employed owners pay payroll tax on their own earnings.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Social Security Board and the National Health Insurance (NHI)
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people must contribute to both.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Prepare payroll tax, Social Security and NHI for your employees
launchSteps.plain: With employees you pay all three every month, by the 15th of the following month.

incomeTax.label: Payroll tax
incomeTax.allowanceNote: the first US$10,000 a year is exempt
incomeTax.bracketText: 10% of earnings above US$10,000 (14% if you employ 7 or more people)

contributions.label: Social Security
contributions.plain: Social Security gives access to a pension and other benefits. Self-employed people pay 8.5% of their earnings, up to US$53,400 a year.

contributions.label: National Health Insurance (NHI)
contributions.plain: NHI covers health care. Self-employed people pay both shares: 7.5% of their earnings, up to US$106,800 a year.

calendar.monthlyText: Pay payroll tax, Social Security and NHI for your employees by the 15th of the following month.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: File your payroll tax return with the Inland Revenue Department.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay payroll tax, Social Security and NHI for the previous month, by the 15th.

notes: The British Virgin Islands has no income tax and no sales tax. Self-employed owners pay payroll tax on their own earnings above US$10,000, plus Social Security and NHI.
Payroll tax for a business with fewer than 7 employees: 10% of pay above US$10,000 per employee (8% deducted from the employee, 2% paid by the employer).
